patterns.prevention:
• Audit coach engagement and energy levels at all centres within 48 hours, documenting baseline performance standards against top performers like Brendan.

• Implement a transition protocol requiring incoming coaches to shadow their predecessor for at least 2 sessions before taking over, and communicate replacement plans to centres 2 weeks in advance.

• Create a backup coach roster at each centre so no programme stops due to a single coach absence or resignation.

patterns.prevention:
• Contact centres that merged or consolidated operations to understand their consolidation timeline and offer bundled pricing for multiple locations before they commit to in-house alternatives.

• Schedule quarterly business reviews with all active centres to identify budget concerns early and present cost-saving options before they explore switching providers.

• Develop a retention offer for centres expressing satisfaction but considering internal programs—position your coaches as specialists they'd need to hire and train versus the cost of running programs in-house.

• Document feedback from centres citing "time didn't work" to identify scheduling gaps in your standard offering and create flexible session timing options as a competitive advantage.
